experiment.name: phase1_domain_split
description: Where in the package does the operand-movement effect sit -- the cores, or
the uncore? And does that answer change with the depth the operand is drawn
from? This is critique item B1.3: the package RAPL counter is never checked
against anything, and its sub-domains are a free internal cross-check plus a
mechanism result.
This part exposes two package sub-domains besides the package counter: PP0
(MSR 0x639, 'core' -- the P/E cores and their caches on a client SKU) and
PP1 (MSR 0x641, client graphics, idle here). The driver now records both at
every RAPL edge, so every condition difference can be read in three domains:
package, core (PP0), and uncore (package minus core). analysis.domains prints
the split; analysis.report enforces the usual gates unchanged.
Two things this buys. (1) Cross-validation: if the package effect also shows
up cleanly and reproducibly in the independently metered PP0 counter, the
package number is structured rather than a flat activity estimate -- the
RAPL-internal complement to the tier-3 timing check (which needs no RAPL at
all) and the battery cross-check (a different instrument entirely). (2)
Mechanism: which rail carries the leak, and whether it migrates toward the
uncore at DRAM depth, where the memory controller does the most work.
Design: the hw32-against-zero contrast (0 vs 0xFFFFFFFF, the canonical
+1.9 W L3 effect) at three depths -- L1, L3, DRAM -- plus the L3 A/A gate and
the standard HW-16 anchor for cross-session comparison. Driver settings match
phase1_hamming_weight exactly (threads 4, 150 blocks, 120 samples, settle 8),
so l3_hw32's package delta must reproduce that session's hw32 (+1.90 W) and
the anchor must land near the corpus's +1.133/+1.215/+1.228/+1.160 W. That
reproduction IS the success criterion: the split must not move the package
number, only decompose it.
warmup_blocks is raised for DRAM: ws_dram_x8 faults in far more under
MAP_POPULATE than the L1/L3 variants, and the run-level transient is real.
Config-A throughout: the split is a power question, and pinning the frequency
keeps a DVFS response from confounding it. work_balance still applies -- at
DRAM the heavier operand tends to move ~2% more bytes, and that qualification
carries over to the domain figures exactly as it does to the package one.

runs.label: aa_l3
runs.comment: A/A gate; every domain delta must sit at zero.

runs.label: l1_hw32
runs.comment: Smallest effect (~+0.17 W); is even that core-localised?

runs.label: l3_hw32
runs.comment: Canonical +1.90 W effect; package delta must reproduce phase1_hamming_weight.

runs.label: dram_hw32
runs.comment: Does the uncore share rise here, where the IMC does the most work?
